## Summary

Test-first contract for the follow-source interface and unlock/persistence logic using a mocked Steamworks session, written before the implementation features (F3/F4). Defines the interface the renderer and unlock logic consume so the Steam SDK stays behind an abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mockable `FollowSource` interface is defined (init, isSteamAvailable, openStorePage, isFollowing, claim) with a deterministic fake implementation.
- [ ] Unit tests (`tests/steam-follow/`) cover: follow detected → unlock flow triggered; already-unlocked → no re-verification prompt; Steam absent → graceful degraded path (no crash); choose-one-of-three catalog resolution; unlock persistence round-trip across simulated launches.
- [ ] Tests run and pass under `--project unit` (fast, no browser).
- [ ] The interface contract documents that the renderer never imports the Steam SDK directly.

## Minimal Implementation

- Test-only feature: interface + test doubles + unit tests.
- Reference the launcher item's content-locator abstraction (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) for the dependency-injection pattern.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher) for the abstraction pattern it establishes.

## Deliverables

- `FollowSource` interface + mocked unit tests.

## Summary

Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron main process: init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap, graceful degradation when Steam is absent, and a minimal preload context-bridge API so the renderer never touches the SDK directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `electron/main.ts` initialises Steamworks (with `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary` + app ID bootstrap, e.g. `steam_appid.txt`) and logs a clear warning when Steam is unavailable.
- [ ] The launcher boots and is fully functional without Steam (dev / non-Steam runs) — no crash, web app unaffected (intake AC5).
- [ ] `electron/preload.ts` exposes a minimal `steamFollow` API via contextBridge: `isSteamAvailable`, `openStorePage(appId)`, `isFollowing(devAccountId)`, `claim(...)` (as confirmed by F1).
- [ ] Renderer code has zero direct Steam SDK imports (enforced by F2's interface contract).
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds with the Steamworks native module packaging config (Windows primary target per launcher item).
- [ ] All F2 unit tests still pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Steamworks init module behind the `FollowSource` interface (F2).
- Preload context bridge exposing `steamFollow`.
- electron-builder config updated for the native module (Windows primary).

## Dependencies

- F2 (interface contract).
- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher provides electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts structure).

## Deliverables

- `electron/main.ts` Steamworks init, `electron/preload.ts` bridge, packaging config.

data.description:
## Goal

Add the failing unit tests that pin the capacity-template contract (parent AC1–AC6) **before** the `HandView` fix lands, so the regression is captured as an executable specification.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Test-first item.

Today `HandView.computeCardPositions()` builds one row centred on the **current** `cards.length`, and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts that row; adding a card therefore re-centres every card and every outline. The fix (sibling item) will derive positions from `maxSlots`. These tests must be red against the current code and green once the fix lands.

The existing Phaser mock in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (mock `scene.add.rectangle` / `image` / `text`) is the harness to reuse; assert on `scene._rectangles` (outlines), `handView` sprites, and `outlineRects`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1: with `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each size) — asserted as a unit test in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`.
- Parent AC2: adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured: for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`) — asserted for successive adds up to capacity and for successive `setCards` growth.
- Parent AC3: occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
- Parent AC4: changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
- Parent AC5: the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots` straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
- Parent AC6: unit tests verify AC 1–5, including a regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does re-layout.
- Rotation/arc stability: per-card rotation and arc Y are derived from the capacity template, so they do not change when a card is added (assert `sprite.rotation` unchanged for pre-existing cards).
- `getInsertionPosition(i)` equals the rendered sprite position after inserting at `i` (guards the Main Street market→hand transfer).
- Over-capacity (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) is best-effort: the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`, overflow cards continue to the right with the same step.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout (regression guard), and vertical cascade (already count-independent) is unchanged.
- Run via `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (unit profile).

**Key Files:**

- `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` — extend with the stability/regression cases (existing Phaser mock harness).
- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — read-only reference for the API under test.

**Deliverables:**

- Failing-then-passing automated regression tests in the `unit` profile.
data.title: Unit tests: capacity slots stay fixed

data.description:
# Create Gym DPR comparison scene showing native-resolution SVG rendering at DPR 1, 2 and 3

## Problem statement

The SvgHelpers module rasterises card SVGs at `Math.max(MIN_QUALITY_SCALE, dpr)` quality scale, but developers have no interactive way to observe how the same SVG renders at different device pixel ratios. A Gym comparison scene will make the DPR-dependent resolution contract visually verifiable.

## Users

- **Engine developers / QA** — want to visually verify that DPR 1, 2, 3 renderings are correct at a glance, without writing unit tests.
- **Producers** — want a quick visual sign-off that the new 2x floor does not regress legibility at any DPR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scene is selectable from the Gym Router** and navigable via Prev/Next buttons.
2. **Three side-by-side panels** show the same SVG rasterised at DPR 1, 2, 3. Each panel is labelled with its DPR, quality scale, logical size, canvas dimensions and resulting display size.
3. **All three panels share the same logical display size** so the quality difference is immediately apparent (e.g. 140×80 logical rendered at 280×160 @ DPR 1, 280×160 @ DPR 2, 420×240 @ DPR 3 — all displayed at the same 140×80 image size).
4. **A zoom/crop toggle** lets the user inspect a 2× cropped region at native resolution (each panel shows a 2× zoom of a detail area).
5. **Scene follows Gym conventions**: extends `GymSceneBase`, registered in `GymRegistry`/`GYM_SCENE_CATALOGUE`, uses SLL layout (no hardcoded pixel positions), has help panel, supports reduced-motion.
6. **Unit and browser smoke tests** verify scene registration and basic rendering.
7. **`docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`** updated with the new scene entry.
8. **Full project test suite passes**.

## Constraints

- Reuses `SvgHelpers` exports (`rasteriseSvgToTexture`, `markSceneValid`, `MIN_QUALITY_SCALE`).
- No external assets needed — uses the tempura icon from the existing `GymSvgHelpersScene` or a simple inline SVG.
- SLL layout (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- Reduced-motion aware.

## Related work

- **CG-0MUCMB8DT003DAKR** — Render card SVGs at native resolution (just shipped to dev; this scene validates the change visually).
- **CG-0MQK9ZMCI0043712** — Gym: SvgHelpers demo scene (existing; this is a companion scene with a different teaching goal).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymDprResolutionScene.ts` — new scene
- `example-games/gym/GymRegistry.ts` — register new scene
- `tests/gym/` — new smoke test
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — new scene entry
data.title: Create Gym DPR comparison scene showing native-resolution SVG rendering at DPR 1, 2 and 3
